_meta.description: Bounded, redacted sample of the operator's personal work-queue corpus (~/work-queue), used by tests/router/test_classifier_coverage_ratchet.py as a CI-visible input to classify.py's route classifier. Each item is focus text (the same field the classifier reads live) plus the route the brief was ACTUALLY run under, read from the selected_route of a run record that consumed it. Briefs labelled only by their own recommended-route frontmatter are excluded: that is a machine suggestion, not an outcome, and scoring classify.py against it measures agreement with a guess. label_source records this per item so the distinction survives the next regeneration.
_meta.sampling: Stratified: up to 24 items per route (A-J), evenly spaced across each route's available pool. Outcome labels are rare, so most routes fall well under the cap and a route with no outcome-labelled brief is absent entirely. Uneven counts are accepted rather than padded with frontmatter guesses.

the-repo: systematic gate-parity audit between the one-off /go path and the orchestrator group-PR path. MOTIVATION: three confirmed instances of one shape, each found incidentally rather than by design. (1) require_human_routes/gates never threaded into integrate.py's _refresh_pr_labels subprocess call (brief <brief-id>, picked). (2) classify.py's bounded-autonomy gates largely prose-only with no mechanical consumer (docs/specs/research/classify-gate-enforcement-audit.md, which notes at :75-78 that the orchestrator calls pre_pr_gate.py --labels-only but does not follow that thread to its consequences). (3) VERIFIED 2026-08-15: --labels-only returns at pre_pr_gate.py:352-361 before spec-sync, clarification-integrity, DoD-verification, and req/AC-coverage, so no orchestrator group PR runs any of them (brief <brief-id> covers that instance's fix). The pattern: a policy or drift gate gets wired into the-repo-preflight/pre_pr_gate.py for the one-off route, and the orchestrator's separate raw-subprocess PR path (integrate.py, which live.py:111-115 notes is unreachable by any Claude Code hook, headless or interactive) silently does not inherit it. Because orchestrated runs produce most merged PRs across the-repo/the-repo/the-repo, the path with the weakest enforcement is the one carrying the most volume. SCOPE: enumerate every gate, drift check, policy verdict, and approval requirement reachable on the one-off path (the-repo-preflight run, pre_pr_gate.py main, classify.py gates, policy.py automerge_eligible/require_human_routes/protected_paths, run_record scope-completeness) and, for each, establish by source read whether it reaches integrate.py's group-PR path, is deliberately exempt with a recorded reason, or is silently skipped. Deliverables: (1) a parity matrix committed under docs/specs/research/ listing gate x one-off-enforced x orchestrator-enforced x verdict; (2) a brief per genuine gap found; (3) the durable part -- a regression test or selfcheck that fails when a NEW gate is added to the one-off path without an explicit orchestrator-path decision, so instance four is caught by CI instead of by a human reading source months later. That last deliverable is the real value: the audit closes today's gaps, the selfcheck closes the pattern. Consider modelling it on the existing *_selfcheck.py family (policy_selfcheck, policy_drift_selfcheck, journal_selfcheck, automerge_selfcheck) which already establishes the convention of a cheap deterministic check wired into pre_pr_gate.py. Sequence AFTER brief <brief-id> so the audit measures the post-fix baseline rather than re-finding the same instance.
